@asadmalik901  @kiril\_dobrev the frame rate at export handles one half of this, but the earlier problem is placing the note in the first place. if a reviewer is scrubbing a youtube embed to leave a comment, they're limited by whatever seek precision that player gives them, so the timestamp going in could already be a frame or two off before frame rate even enters into it. is there a way to nudge a placed note frame by frame after the fact, or is initial placement stuck at whatever precision the source player allows

Report

Asad M. [...] Report

Asad M.

@kiril\_dobrev  @raffay\_sajjad Right, and that's the bigger half. Reading the position is easy, getCurrentTime hands you a float. It's the seek that snaps, so the reviewer can't land where they meant to. The fix isn't better seeking, it's letting them nudge the note after placement with arrow keys stepping one frame, which means asking for frame rate up front rather than at export. Kiril already collects it, just at the wrong end of the workflow.
